counts_source.locator: PDF p. 4, section 3.2 (reported total participant sample and random assignment of all selected students); PDF p. 9, Table 1 (analyzed Group and N cells). Quote contains separate excerpts in that order.
counts_source.quote:
A total of 120 students aged between 19 and 22 years (M = 20.4, SD = 0.84) participated in the experiment.
(1) GAI-SDTS 40
(2) GAI 40
(3) TDL 40

arms.name: GAI-SDTS
arms.description: Deepseek and Dreamina with a Double Diamond-Based Design Operation Sheet guiding Discover, Define, Develop, and Deliver; operational tool training preceded the design tasks (PDF p. 5, section 3.3; PDF p. 8, section 3.5).

arms.name: GAI
arms.description: Free use of the same Deepseek and Dreamina tools without structured design-thinking guidance; the same operational tool training as GAI-SDTS (PDF p. 5, section 3.3; PDF p. 8, section 3.5).

arms.name: TDL
arms.description: Traditional design learning with printed and online references, hand-drawn sketches, and conventional software such as Photoshop, without generative AI or explicit design-thinking guidance (PDF p. 5, section 3.3).

studies.task: Second-year animation undergraduates independently created a distinctive card-game character with clear personality traits during a university character-design course (PDF p. 4, sections 3.2-3.3).

ai_tool.name: Deepseek and Dreamina
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5, section 3.3; PDF p. 8, section 3.5. Release years are not stated; the model versions used throughout the experiment are not established.

estimates.outcome: Design achievement: expert-rated composite of final character artwork
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two design instructors independently rated anonymized, randomly ordered final artwork. The rubric covers Technical Skill; Adherence to Theme; Composition and Design; Creativity; and Detail Quality and Workload. Each dimension uses a five-point Likert scale, from 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest). The aggregation across dimensions and raters is not specified (PDF p. 8, section 3.4).

sources.locator: PDF p. 9, Table 1, post-test GAI row; Group, N, Mean, S.D. cells.
PDF p. 9, Table 1, post-test TDL row; Group, N, Mean, S.D. cells.
PDF p. 9, section 4.1, Tukey HSD pairwise-comparisons sentence.

estimates.notes: This is the broad design-quality composite, coded usefulness; the Creativity rubric dimension is not separately reported. The analysis uses one design-achievement score per student; Table 1 reports participant counts and SDs, and sections 4-4.1 describe one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey HSD. The p_value is the printed pairwise Tukey bound. The reported F is an omnibus test across all study arms, so stats.test is null. The printed arm summaries and pairwise significance appear inconsistent; they are preserved without correction or calculation. No pair-specific total N is printed, so n_total is null rather than calculated from the arm counts. No numerical pairwise difference, SE, confidence interval, or standardized effect is printed. The artwork was produced with AI available in the AI arms and graded at course end; this is immediate assisted production, not a new delayed or unassisted task (PDF p. 9, section 3.5; PDF p. 11, section 5.1).

not_extracted.reason: Self-report questionnaire measuring confidence in creative ability, not a score on produced artwork (PDF p. 8, section 3.4; PDF p. 10, section 4.2 and Table 2). All group comparisons are excluded.

Self-reported creative-ideas confidence, a CSE subscale; not an output-based creativity or idea-count measure (PDF p. 8, section 3.4; PDF p. 10, section 4.2 and Table 2). All group comparisons are excluded.

not_extracted.what: S1: Separate Technical Skill, Adherence to Theme, Composition and Design, Creativity, and Detail Quality and Workload scores
not_extracted.reason: These dimensions are named in the design-achievement rubric, but no separate dimension results or contrasts are printed. Table 1 reports only the combined design-achievement outcome; all of its reported pairwise contrasts are extracted (PDF p. 8, section 3.4; PDF p. 9, Table 1 and section 4.1).

open_items: The Table 1 arm means, SDs and sample sizes appear inconsistent with the omnibus ANOVA and all-pairs Tukey significance reported in section 4.1 (PDF p. 9). No underlying participant data, corrected statistics or numerical pairwise uncertainty are supplied. Values are transcribed unchanged; no replacement statistics are computed.

The rule for combining rubric dimensions and instructor ratings is not supplied. Separate results for Creativity and the other rubric dimensions are not printed (PDF p. 8, section 3.4; PDF p. 9, Table 1). The extracted outcome is the reported composite only.

Sequence generation and allocation implementation are not described. The paper labels the design quasi-experimental but explicitly reports random assignment of individual students and regrouping across sampled classes (PDF pp. 3-4, sections 3.1-3.2).

Figure 1 labels design achievement ANCOVA and the questionnaire outcomes ANOVA, reversing the Results and table titles. Extraction follows the explicit one-way ANOVA for design achievement in section 4 and Table 1 (PDF p. 4, Figure 1; PDF pp. 9-11, sections 4-4.3 and Tables 1-3).

The experiment-wide Deepseek and Dreamina model versions and release years are unconfirmed. Illustrated Dreamina interface labels do not establish versions used throughout the experiment (PDF p. 7, Figure 6; PDF p. 8, Figure 7; PDF p. 5, section 3.3). ai_tool.year is null.

The external Supplementary Table S1 was not independently retrieved in this reconciliation. The main text identifies it as the Double Diamond-Based Design Operation Sheet (PDF p. 5, section 3.3), and PDF p. 14 gives the publisher supplement link. The existing forms/data/c566.json inventory reports an earlier complete inspection of a materials-only DOCX, with no outcome statistics; that inventory is secondary evidence. Current urllib requests using User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 to https://www.frontiersin.org/api/v4/articles/1847432/supplemental-data, https://api.figshare.com/v2/articles/32695107, https://public-pages-files-2025.frontiersin.org/articles/1847432/file/Table_1.docx/1847432_table_1/1, and https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/65613543 all failed with WinError 10013. No supplement-only numbers are assumed.

The paper does not print pairwise mean differences, SEs, confidence intervals, standardized effects or pair-specific total participant counts for design achievement (PDF p. 9, Table 1 and section 4.1). These fields remain null.
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-11. The extraction specification and codebook were read before the paper. The complete markdown conversion was read in consecutive chunks through the final reference. Every cited PDF page was extracted with pymupdf; Table 1 was also recovered with find_tables. Figures 1 and 8 were inspected in memory, and illustrated Dreamina interface information was checked without creating files. The PDF has no appended supplement or embedded attachment. Both extractor files, the full difference inventory, the screening outcome/contrast map, citation record, sample-overlap field, and screening open items were checked. The two difference-inventory entries are settled in resolutions. Neither extractor has an unmatched estimate. All three contrasts of S1-O1 are present; no eligible estimate was missed by both extractors. The separate rubric dimensions are additionally listed in not_extracted because no dimension-specific results are printed. Shared fields were independently checked: the reported study sample is 120 students, all selected students were randomly assigned, and Table 1 reports an analyzed N of 40 per arm. The study total uses the stated participant sample; the paper reports no separate exclusions, attrition, or intention-to-treat accounting. Initial arm-allocation counts occur only in Figure 8 (PDF p. 9), so arm n_randomized remains null under extraction rule 1, without substituting analyzed counts. Pair-specific n_total remains null because none is printed. Classes were sampled before individual assignment; sampling classes are not randomized clusters, and the paper does not establish session-level assignment. Design achievement is a broad expert-rated output-quality composite including a Creativity dimension, coded usefulness. The paper analyzes one design-achievement score per student, so unit, sd_level and se_basis are participant. Higher scores indicate better design quality, represented by higher_is more_creative under the permitted vocabulary. The scored artwork was created with AI available in the AI arms, giving question with_ai and outcome_with_ai true. Course-end grading of this artwork is immediate; there is no new unassisted output or stated delay in days. This is a between-person design, so within_person is null. Deepseek supported text dialogue, ideation, prompts and design statements; Dreamina supported image generation and refinement. Model release years and experiment-wide versions are not confirmed. TDL students used printed materials and online resources to develop character information; these alternative non-AI reference aids make both TDL contrasts ai_vs_active under codebook section 5 (PDF p. 5, section 3.3). GAI-SDTS is the tested configuration in the ai_design contrast against free GAI use. All estimates share the same study sample and reuse comparison arms. No pooled-AI contrast, across-people diversity result, unassisted after-AI output, preregistration, designated primary outcome, or shared sample with another paper is reported. The raw-data statement promises author provision without supplying a public data or code URL (PDF p. 14). Omnibus ANOVA, Levene diagnostics, and inter-rater reliability are not pairwise effects and are not attached to the contrast statistics. Printed outcome summaries and pairwise p-values are preserved despite the unresolved consistency concern. Source quotes retain printed decimal precision and normalize PDF line wraps and whitespace. No effect sizes, standard errors, mean differences, or totals of contrast arms were calculated.

resolutions.decision: Use {} as in A: cluster counts are not applicable to the reported individual random assignment. The classes were sampling units, not randomized treatment clusters; the paper does not establish session-level assignment. The empty mapping follows the extraction structure without inventing cluster counts.
resolutions.locator: PDF p. 4, sections 3.1-3.2, especially Population and sampling.
resolutions.quote: A single-stage cluster sampling method was used to select three classes out of six existing animation classes. All students in the selected classes were then randomly assigned to one of three groups:

a.name: GAI-SDTS
a.description: Deepseek and Dreamina with a Double Diamond-Based Design Operation Sheet guiding Discover, Define, Develop, and Deliver; operational tool training preceded the design tasks (PDF p. 5, section 3.3; PDF p. 8, section 3.5).

a.name: GAI
a.description: Free use of the same Deepseek and Dreamina tools without structured design-thinking guidance; the same operational tool training as GAI-SDTS (PDF p. 5, section 3.3; PDF p. 8, section 3.5).

a.name: TDL
a.description: Traditional design learning with printed and online references, hand-drawn sketches, and conventional software such as Photoshop, without generative AI or explicit design-thinking guidance (PDF p. 5, section 3.3).

b.name: GAI-SDTS
b.description: Generative AI-supported learning with Structured Design Thinking Strategy: Deepseek and Dreamina plus the Double Diamond-Based Design Operation Sheet, guiding Discover, Define, Develop, and Deliver. Same operational AI training as GAI (PDF pp. 5-9, sections 3.3-3.5).

b.name: GAI
b.description: Generative AI-supported learning without the strategy: free use of the same Deepseek and Dreamina tools without structured design-thinking guidance. Same operational AI training as GAI-SDTS (PDF pp. 5-9, sections 3.3-3.5).

b.name: TDL
b.description: Traditional Design Learning: printed materials and online references, hand-drawn sketches, and conventional digital tools such as Photoshop, without generative AI or an explicit design-thinking strategy (PDF pp. 4-5, sections 3.2-3.3).

resolutions.decision: Retain A's arm records: n_randomized is null for each arm because initial arm counts can only be read from Figure 8, which extraction rule 1 excludes. Do not substitute Table 1 analyzed counts for randomized counts. Retain n_analyzed = 40 for each arm from Table 1. Both descriptions correctly identify the interventions; A's wording is retained.
resolutions.locator: PDF p. 9, Figure 8 initial group labels (inspected in the PDF image) and Table 1 Group/N cells; PDF p. 5, section 3.3 and PDF p. 8, section 3.5 for interventions. Extraction specification rule 1 excludes figure-only counts. Quote contains separate figure-label and table-cell excerpts.
